judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Plain, slightly stiff welcomes built around the shop's name and a rival's ('not as fancy as [Person]'s'); no joke reaching for effect. Reads like Westwood's functional greeters.

items.label: B
items.critique: Every line is a crafted punchline (wipe your boots, horseshoes for everybody else, what doesn't sell I drink). Funny, but too evenly joke-loaded across three shops to be Westwood's mix.

items.label: C
items.critique: A terse inn line, a long, awkwardly pushy sales pitch tied to the chapter's trial, and a flat informational magic-shop line. That unevenness and the sales-flyer grammar ('during [Place] run') are Westwood's.

items.label: D
items.critique: Menacing, odd ('arrange funerary services or... purchase goods?') and the abrupt 'Let's get to know each other! Buy something!' have Nox's off-kilter humour without a set-up-and-punchline shape.

items.label: E
items.critique: The 'finest in all of Nox! Well... finest in [Place]' self-correction and 'I also mend cauldrons' side-trade joke are a modern comic formula; 'Sit yerself down' dialect spelling feels added.

items.label: F
items.critique: The side-trade gag again ('I pull teeth too'), and the magic shop line paraphrases a Westwood supplier line too closely ('sole purveyor... State your needs'). Pattern-built.

items.label: G
items.critique: The rambling insult ('pig-headed armored sheep marching up and down, up and down!') and the drawn-out 'Ahhhhhhhh... young sir!' are idiosyncratic and tied to plot, very Westwood.

items.label: H
items.critique: 'Victuallers to the garrison' is a writerly word, 'since the dead started walking' is world-state exposition, and 'goats out back' is a random-comedy beat; three different registers stitched together.

items.label: I
items.critique: Each line explains local circumstance (roads closed, hamlet's swords) and ends with a crafted gag ('still got both your eyebrows'). The em-dash '--' and polished timing give it away.

items.label: J
items.critique: Short, functional, a bit gruff ('be quick about it'), with the shop identifying itself by owner's name. Unpolished in the way Westwood's minor vendors are.

tells: Generated shopkeepers almost all carry a constructed joke per line, especially the 'I also do some unrelated trade' gag (mend cauldrons, pull teeth, horseshoes); Westwood's vendors are often flat or functional, with humour that is odd rather than set-up-and-punchline.
Generated lines explain the town's situation in passing (roads closed, dead walking, half the street gone); Westwood greetings tie to the player's chapter goal or simply name the shop.
Writerly vocabulary (victuallers, purveyor) and '--' dashes mark the new texts; Westwood uses '...' and long drawn-out interjections ('Ahhhhhhhh...').
Westwood's set is uneven in length within one text (a two-word inn line beside a long sales pitch); the generated sets are evenly balanced.
